paper_summary: Metal matrix syntactic foams were produced by low-pressure (500 kPa argon) infiltration of molten A356 aluminium (7Si-0.3Mg) at 840 C into a mixture of Glober Al2O3 ceramic hollow spheres (2.29 +- 0.16 mm) and 20 wt% ceramic reinforcing grains, then T6 heat treated. Four reinforcements were compared with a non-reinforced reference: FS 18, FS 40 and FS 46 Al2O3 grains and FS 46 SiC grains. Quasi-static compression tests to ISO 13314:2011 show the matrix reinforcement always raises compressive strength (by more than 17 % on average, from 108.2 MPa to 116.4-133.8 MPa) but generally lowers the energy absorbed up to 50 % strain; FS 18 Al2O3 performed best.

extraction_notes: All five records come from Table 2 (density, compressive strength sigma_c, and absorbed energy up to 50 % strain W50), one per material variant; values are means +- standard deviation and only the means were extracted. Unit handling: W50 given in J/cm3 is numerically identical to MJ/m3, so it was copied directly into energy_absorption_mj_m3; densities were already g/cm3; reinforcement grain sizes were left in the additional_fillers text in mm as reported. Plateau stress (defined in Sec. 2.3 as the mean stress between 10 % and 40 % strain) and modulus are NOT tabulated - they appear only in the Fig. 6 curves - so those fields are null. Hollow-sphere volume fraction is not reported (only the 20 wt% reinforcement content, which is a matrix reinforcement rather than the hollow filler, so it was recorded in additional_fillers and not in particle_weight_fraction). Test temperature is not stated (ambient assumed but left null) and the strain rate was left null because the specimen height corresponding to the 4 mm/min cross-head speed is ambiguous (blocks of 30x30x40 mm and 10 mm cubes are both mentioned); the cross-head speed is recorded in specimen_notes. cure_or_process_temperature_c = 840 C is the melt pouring temperature; the moulds were preheated to 600 C for 1 h and specimens were subsequently T6 heat treated (535 C / 4 h + 150 C / 15 h), noted in matrix_name.
